title_original: Iranian ‘Happy Ending’ filmmakers prevented from travelling to Tallinn world premiere
excerpt_original: Filmmaking team have passports confiscated by Iranian authorities.

blocks.text: The Iranian filmmakers behind Happy Ending , which world premiered last night (November 17) in Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival’s (PÖFF) first feature competition, were unable to travel to the event after their passports were seized by Iranian authorities.

According to sources associated with the production but based outside Iran, the film’s cast and crew, as well as the director and the producer, a total of 15 people, were prevented from travelling to the festival.
The news comes just days after reports that Palme d’Or-winning director Jafar Panahi is facing a five-year prison sentence in Iran.

links.text: Jafar Panahi is facing a five-year prison sentence

blocks.text: Happy Ending , directed by Atena Mahmoudi and produced by Abdolreza Heydari, is the story of a literature student who is working illegally as a masseuse in a private flat. News of her magical hands spread through Tehran, and men with ties to the government book appointments, some hoping for a “happy ending”.
It was filmed “guerrilla style” in private flats.
“[The authorities] attacked the producer’s office and confiscated everything they had – the rushes, the audio, and even their laptops and hard drives,” the source stated.
The filmmakers had anticipated their film would be “sensitive” to the regime and therefore sent the rushes outside Iran.

“For that reason, they were able to reassemble the edit not only once or twice but three times,” said the source, who explained the filmmakers edited new versions after the authorities kept on confiscating the film.
“The team had sent abroad an unfinished copy of the film and that’s how they managed to finish it and send it to us,” a POFF representative confirmed.
In the absence of the cast and filmmakers, project consultant Mohammad Ravandi, composer Hossein Mirzagholi and poster designer Diako Ravandi represented Happy Ending in Tallinn.

Happy Ending producer Heydari was the sound designer on Ali Asgari’s Divine Comedy , which has been screening as a Critics’ Choice at POFF. He also produced Ava Shahnavaz’s A Spinner , which screened in the shorts live action competition at POFF, and was part of the sound team on such films as Panahi’s It Was Just An Accident and My Favourite Cake directed by Maryam Moqhaddam and Behtash Sanaeeha.
